The record:
Write the overview of the executive synopsis for the incident on io-shop below: a short paragraph in plain words, for the people who lead the company rather than the engineers who responded - what happened, how long it lasted, what it cost the business and the people who responded, and how it was resolved.

What a reader saw: Shoppers' account pages failed to load
Why, in plain words: An admin switched on a new monthly spending summary for shoppers' account pages, and its calculation then failed with a division by zero, most likely for shoppers who had bought before but nothing yet this month, so their account pages failed to load.

Figures:
- How long it lasted: 7m 2s {duration}
- Requests failing at the worst minute: 40.5% {peak_error_rate}
- What it cost the shop in takings (estimated by Argus): 5,194.52 USD {customer_loss}
- People who responded: 2 {responders}
- Their time, added together: 17 min {engineer_minutes}
- What their time cost: {responder_cost} (its amount is not shown to you; name it where it goes)

What was done to end it:
- Argus: reverted the feature flag monthly-spend-feature - confirmed, still in place
- Argus: proposed a fix, PR #579 - opened as a draft

Name {duration}, {customer_loss} and {responder_cost} in your overview.
Write no figure yourself - not in digits, not spelled out, and not as a word that sizes it ("a brief outage", "a minor loss", "tripled"). Where a figure goes, write its name, braces and all, and the synopsis writes the figure in.
Say nothing about how the incident was resolved beyond what the list of what was done says: a draft fix has not run, and nothing it would do has happened.
Speak of Argus by name, never as "we", "our" or "us": Argus is the system that responded, and each line of what was done says who did it.
Where you say who was affected, say which ones, as the cause does, or that some were, where it does not say which - never how many, and never all of them, where the cause does not say all.
Keep "likely" on what the cause says is likely, and only there.

Call submit_executive_overview with your overview.

The postmortem it is written from:
Shoppers' account pages failed to load while monthly-spend-feature was on
Incident: HighErrorRate on io-shop
Date: Nov 12, 2026, 19:52 to 19:59:02 UTC
Status: Draft. 1 of 6 action items are done.
Written by: Argus Postmortem agent, Nov 12, 2026, 20:19:31 UTC. Not reviewed yet. Each part is as of when the work it reports ended, which the timeline dates; who ended the incident is as of now.
First told: Argus posted in Slack, Nov 12, 2026, 19:58:27 UTC
Ended by: Argus: reverted the feature flag monthly-spend-feature - confirmed, still in place

Summary
The service broke at 19:52 UTC and was back to normal at 19:59:02 UTC, 7 minutes 2 seconds later. 32.6% of requests failed while it was broken, against 0.9% before it began. At its worst, 40.5% failed. The shop's takings fell short of the same hours on earlier weeks by 5,194.52 USD, beyond how much those hours vary on their own. An admin switched on a new monthly spending summary for shoppers' account pages, and its calculation then failed with a division by zero, most likely for shoppers who had bought before but nothing yet this month, so their account pages failed to load. What Argus did: reverted the feature flag monthly-spend-feature (can be put back) - confirmed, still in place. Argus opened a draft fix, PR #579, for a person to review and merge. Switching the monthly-spend-feature flag back on would likely make account pages fail again for shoppers with no purchases this month.

Impact
7m 2s - onset until back to normal
40.5% - peak error rate
2,742 - requests failed
0.9% to 32.6% - what the alert watches, before onset and while broken on average (the rule's line is 10%)
5,194.52 USD - customer loss (estimated)

Root cause and contributing factors
With monthly-spend-feature on, account page requests reach `average_spend_per_item_this_month` in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py. It integer-divides the month's spend total by the number of purchases marked as this month, and nothing guards against that list being empty. A shopper who has bought before but not this month therefore raises ZeroDivisionError, and the boundary in src/io_shop/account_page.py turns that error into a failed page. It rests on F1, a reading of the source nothing ran, so it is unverified.
Causal chain
symptom Shoppers' account page requests failed, and the logs report a rising account-page error rate.
  Evidence:
    G5309 ERROR io-shop: account page request failed - ZeroDivisionError: division by zero at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47 - 14 occurrences in 7 minutes, 19:52–19:58
    Gbac1 WARN io-shop: account page error rate at #% over the last minute - 28 occurrences in 36 minutes, 19:23–19:58; # was 0.50% to 40.50%, typically 1.50%, highest at 19:55
why 1 The failing account page requests raised ZeroDivisionError in the spend summary code (src/io_shop/spend_summary.py). This error first appears in the minute the onset is dated to and was not seen before it.
  Evidence:
    G5309
why 2 The spend summary code ran on account page requests because admin switched the monthly-spend-feature flag on at 19:52:31 UTC. The logs show the flag evaluated off in every minute before that, split between off and on during that minute, and on in every minute after.
  Evidence:
    P1 19:52:31 UTC flag toggle monthly-spend-feature by admin: feature flag monthly-spend-feature was switched on
    G7e5d INFO io-shop: monthly-spend-feature=off - 200 evaluations - 30 occurrences in 30 minutes, 19:22–19:51
    G971b INFO io-shop: monthly-spend-feature=off 101 / on 99 - 200 evaluations - 1 occurrence in 1 minute, 19:52
    Gce95 INFO io-shop: monthly-spend-feature=on - 200 evaluations - 6 occurrences in 6 minutes, 19:53–19:58
  Ruled out:
    A deploy or release on the service: the Investigator Agent asked for production change events - deploys and releases, and flag changes from the flag provider's history, the 1 day 1 minute before Nov 12 19:53; the Investigator Agent read back 1 production change.
      T7
      T8
    Another flag change: the flag provider's history showed 1 flag change by anyone but Argus in the 1 hour read, the switch of monthly-spend-feature.
      T14 19:58:51 Argus: Read the flag provider's history - 1 flag change by anyone but Argus, the 1 hour before 19:58:51
    The ClientDisconnected account-page failures: they occurred throughout the minutes before the onset, while the flag was still off.
      G46bc ERROR io-shop: account page request failed - ClientDisconnected: the shopper closed the connection - 37 occurrences in 29 minutes, 19:23–19:51
      G7e5d
why 3 With the flag on, the monthly spend summary divided by the number of the shopper's purchases this month, which is zero for a shopper who has bought before but not this month.
  Evidence:
    F1 What Code-Fix read in the source and proposed - nothing ran its test or its fix
Contributing factors
- No check was seen that would have limited the monthly-spend-feature flag to a small share of shoppers when it was first switched on, or watched errors as it went out. The flag was evaluated on for all traffic soon after the switch. (AI-3, AI-4)
- No test was seen that ran the monthly spend summary for a shopper with no purchases this month before the flag was switched on in production. Code-Fix's reading says its new tests for that case would fail against the current code. (AI-5)
- Code-Fix's reading of src/io_shop/account_page.py says the page's error boundary turned each error from the spend summary into a failed page. Nothing was seen that would render the page without the summary when the summary fails. (AI-6)

Hypotheses considered
 | Hypothesis | Confidence | Result
C1 | The feature flag monthly-spend-feature was switched from off to on at 19:52:31 UTC. The newly enabled spend-summary path then raised ZeroDivisionError at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47 on account page requests, and the error rate rose from about 1% to 20-40%. | 0.93 | confirmed

Trigger
monthly-spend-feature flag went from OFF to ON at 19:52:31 UTC, by admin.

Resolution
 | Time (UTC) | Action | By | Kind | Outcome
M1 | 19:59:02 | Reverted the feature flag monthly-spend-feature for C1 | Argus | can be put back | confirmed, still in place
 | 20:02:55 | Proposed a fix: PR #579 | Code-Fix Agent | nothing to put back | opened as a draft

Detection
The incident on io-shop began at 19:52 UTC. HighErrorRate fired at 19:58:05 UTC, 6 minutes 5 seconds later.
What the alert said
AL1 | Error rate above threshold for 5m

Action items
Item | Action | Type | Owner | Tracking | Status
AI-1 | Reverted the feature flag monthly-spend-feature | mitigate | Argus | - | done
AI-2 | Review and merge the proposed fix | prevent | unassigned | PR #579 | open
AI-3 | Switch monthly-spend-feature, and other new feature flags, on in production gradually, for a growing share of shoppers, and widen it only while the error rate holds at its baseline. | prevent | unassigned | - | open
AI-4 | Switch a feature flag back off automatically when the service's error rate rises soon after the flag is changed. | mitigate | unassigned | - | open
AI-5 | Require the test suite to pass with each new feature flag switched on before that flag can be switched on in production. | process | unassigned | - | open
AI-6 | Make the account page render without the spend summary when computing the summary fails, instead of failing the whole page. | prevent | unassigned | - | open

Lessons learned
What went well
- The alert came within the 7 minutes 30 seconds accounted for by its rule waiting 5 minutes with its condition holding, its evaluation at intervals of 1 minute, an unmeasured allowance of 30 seconds for scraping and storing its samples and the whole minute the onset is measured to.
- 46 seconds after the alert was raised, the Investigator Agent formed 1 candidate cause, best first: C1.
- 57 seconds after the alert was raised, the Mitigation Agent reverted the feature flag monthly-spend-feature for C1, moved from ON to OFF.
- 3 minutes 3 seconds after the alert was raised, the Mitigation Agent judged the action CONFIRMED.
- 4 minutes 50 seconds after the alert was raised, the Code-Fix Agent proposed a fix as a draft pull request - PR #579.
What went wrong
Nothing.
Where it got lucky
Nothing.

Timeline (UTC)
 | Nov 12 19:52 | IMPACT BEGINS | the incident began
 | 19:58:05 | DETECTED | HighErrorRate on io-shop fired
T1 | 19:58:26 |  | Argus Received HighErrorRate on io-shop
T2 | 19:58:42 |  | Argus Moved the incident to INVESTIGATING - a worker took the incident up
T3 | 19:58:42 |  | Investigator Agent Asked for the service's per-minute metrics, anchored on 19:58:05
T4 | 19:58:47 |  | Investigator Agent Read back 360 minutes of metrics
T5 | 19:58:47 |  | Investigator Agent Placed the start of the incident at 19:52
T6 | 19:58:47 |  | Investigator Agent Recorded where the 3 replicas run - all on Tesla-V100-SXM2-16GB
T7 | 19:58:48 |  | Investigator Agent Asked for production change events - deploys and releases, and flag changes from the flag provider's history, the 1 day 1 minute before Nov 12 19:53
T8 | 19:58:49 |  | Investigator Agent Read back 1 production change
T9 | 19:58:49 |  | Investigator Agent Read how far the deployment had rolled out - all 3 replicas run one revision, which the history does not name
T10 | 19:58:49 |  | Investigator Agent Asked for the service's log lines, the 36 minutes 5 seconds before 19:58:05
T11 | 19:58:50 |  | Investigator Agent Read back 125 log lines
T12 | 19:58:51 |  | Investigator Agent Formed 1 candidate cause, best first: C1
T13 | 19:58:51 |  | Investigator Agent Read every channel available
T14 | 19:58:51 |  | Argus Read the flag provider's history - 1 flag change by anyone but Argus, the 1 hour before 19:58:51
T15 | 19:58:52 |  | Argus Moved the incident to MITIGATING to act on a candidate
T16 | 19:59:02 | MITIGATION APPLIED | Mitigation Agent Reverted the feature flag monthly-spend-feature for C1, moved from ON to OFF
 | 19:59:02 | IMPACT ENDS | the service was back to normal
T17 | 19:59:09 |  | Mitigation Agent Waiting to see whether the service is still at the incident's level, from 20:00 - up to 177s
T18 | 20:01:08 |  | Mitigation Agent Looked at the service - no longer at the incident's level since 19:59
T19 | 20:01:08 |  | Mitigation Agent Judged the action CONFIRMED
T20 | 20:01:08 |  | Argus Moved the incident to MITIGATED - set flag monthly-spend-feature OFF and the rule that fired stopped firing
T21 | 20:02:55 |  | Code-Fix Agent Proposed a fix as a draft pull request - PR #579

Response effort
17 min - engineer time, 2 responders (Senior Software Engineer, Site Reliability Engineer)
159,604 - tokens spent by Argus

Supporting information
The incident's walk: http://localhost:8000/incidents/2a48de32-31e3-4cab-8fbb-e009131fc575
The fix it proposed: PR #579 (https://github.com/ohadraz/Argus-Demo-Target-App/pull/579) opened as a draft. The record holds nothing about it after that.
Changes to production read
P1 | 19:52:31 UTC flag toggle monthly-spend-feature by admin: feature flag monthly-spend-feature was switched on
Deploys read, none came back.
Log messages read (UTC)
G7e5d | INFO io-shop: monthly-spend-feature=off - 200 evaluations - 30 occurrences in 30 minutes, 19:22–19:51
Gad41 | INFO io-shop: account pages rendered normally - 9 occurrences in 27 minutes, 19:22–19:48
G46bc | ERROR io-shop: account page request failed - ClientDisconnected: the shopper closed the connection - 37 occurrences in 29 minutes, 19:23–19:51
Gbac1 | WARN io-shop: account page error rate at #% over the last minute - 28 occurrences in 36 minutes, 19:23–19:58; # was 0.50% to 40.50%, typically 1.50%, highest at 19:55
G971b | INFO io-shop: monthly-spend-feature=off 101 / on 99 - 200 evaluations - 1 occurrence in 1 minute, 19:52
G5309 | ERROR io-shop: account page request failed - ZeroDivisionError: division by zero at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47 - 14 occurrences in 7 minutes, 19:52–19:58
Gce95 | INFO io-shop: monthly-spend-feature=on - 200 evaluations - 6 occurrences in 6 minutes, 19:53–19:58
What Code-Fix read in the source and proposed - nothing ran its test or its fix
F1 | The fault: average_spend_per_item_this_month in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py returns account.total_this_month_cents // len(bought_this_month), where bought_this_month is the purchases flagged in_current_month. A shopper who has bought before but not this month has an empty list there, so the line raises ZeroDivisionError. That is not an edge case. tests/io_shop/test_spend_summary.py calls it "the ordinary case". With monthly-spend-feature off, render_spend_summary never reached this function. With it on, every such shopper's request reached it, and the boundary in src/io_shop/account_page.py turned each error into a failed page.

The change: if there are no purchases this month, the function returns 0. Nothing was spent per item this month, and total_this_month_cents is itself 0 for such an account in the fixtures. Otherwise the division is unchanged. With the flag off, nothing changes. average_spend_per_item and the lifetime path are untouched. They still raise for an account that has never bought anything, which the existing tests in tests/io_shop/test_account_page.py and tests/io_shop/test_spend_summary.py rely on. render_spend_summary and serve_account_page still get an int, so their return types and callers are unchanged.

The tests: three new cases in tests/io_shop/test_spend_summary.py. Two call the monthly figure directly and through render_spend_summary(..., use_monthly_summary=True) for a shopper with no purchases this month, and expect 0. One expects 0 for a shopper with no history at all when the monthly flag is on. Each of these would raise ZeroDivisionError against the current code. The test that expects a failure to reach the caller on the lifetime path stays as it is.
Assumptions
- Exchange rate: EUR converted at 0.92191 per USD, published 2026-11-12
- Shared page: the on-call incident this one was paged under was also about 1 other incident, so the engineer minutes are its whole response rather than this incident's share

Review checklist
✓ Key incident data collected (met)
✓ Impact assessed (met)
○ Root-cause analysis complete (for a person)
  running the proposed fix's tests against the current code would confirm the reading, not that the code it reads is what ran (AI-2)
○ Every action item owned and dated (for a person)
○ Reviewed and shared (for a person)

The document, by field:
overview: For {duration}, some shoppers on io-shop could not open their account pages. An admin had switched on a new monthly spending summary for those pages, and its calculation failed with a division by zero. This most likely hit shoppers who had bought before but had bought nothing yet this month. Argus estimates the shop lost {customer_loss} in takings. The time of the people who responded cost {responder_cost}. Argus ended the incident by turning the new feature back off, and it is still off. Argus has also proposed a code fix, but it is only a draft and has not been applied.

Not to be judged:
  - Names in braces, such as {duration}, are figures code writes in from the list of figures in the ask. They are not judged.
  - The overview is written in plain words for the people who lead the company. A claim said more plainly than the postmortem says it is grounded where it means the same.

Judge every claim in the document, and answer by calling judge_claims.

tools.description: Submit every claim in the document, each either as supported or as flagged. Supported: the document's own words, quoted exactly, and the record's rows that support it. Flagged: the document's own words, quoted exactly, why, and the record's rows that contradict it (none where no row speaks to it at all). Empty lists say the document makes no claim to judge.

why.description: One sentence: what the record holds instead. Never empty.
